verdict.rationale: Keycloak's Server Administration Guide documents built-in, per-realm SCIM endpoints for managing users and groups. It covers enabling SCIM for a realm, finding the SCIM base URL, and setting up a service-account client, so a customer directory can push user and group changes into Keycloak, with protected admin users excluded from SCIM. Because Keycloak is the SSO broker for the apps, a SCIM deprovision cuts off login. The evidence does not explicitly show that a SCIM delete or disable terminates active sessions or tokens, though a token revocation endpoint is documented. Missing for 10: documented behavior showing SCIM deprovisioning revokes live sessions and tokens, SCIM operation and attribute coverage details, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the SCIM feature.
